task.title: Multi-day drift audit: 30+ day state, growth, residual, and degradation trends
task.objective: Create a drift audit tool that runs a 30+ simulated-day session and systematically detects unbounded, monotonic, or structurally stuck drift patterns across all tracked dimensions — state values, growth-buffer accumulation, residual stacking, and degradation-rate trends — producing a machine-readable report with per-dimension verdicts.
exact_scope: Create a new audit script (e.g. back/tools/audit_drift.py) that runs 30+ simulated days using the existing advance_day pathway and collects per-day snapshots of: (a) all AgentState numeric fields (moodScore, energy, stress, socialDrive, socialFulfillment, learningState, workState), (b) all AgentGrowth numeric fields (curiosity, caution, socialOpenness, expression, trustInOthers, emotionalStability), (c) pending_residuals count and composition per day from DaySnapshot, (d) DegradationTracker rolling rates and auto-fallback state per tick type if a tracker is provided.

For each tracked dimension, compute and report: (1) monotonic-drift detection — flag any dimension that moves in the same direction for N consecutive days (N configurable, default 10), (2) unbounded-growth detection — flag any dimension whose cumulative delta exceeds a configurable threshold over the run, (3) saturation/floor lock — flag any dimension that stays at its ceiling (>=93) or floor (<=7) for more than M consecutive days (M configurable, default 5), (4) residual stacking — flag if pending_residuals count exceeds a configurable max on any day, or if residual count is monotonically non-decreasing over K consecutive days (K configurable, default 7).

Output a JSON report file containing: per-dimension trajectory arrays, per-dimension drift verdicts (pass/warn/fail with reason), a residual-stacking section, a degradation-trend section (if tracker provided), and a top-level summary with overall pass/fail.

Create a corresponding test file (e.g. back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py) that verifies: (a) the audit script runs to completion on the deterministic backbone for 30 days without error, (b) each drift-detection rule produces correct verdicts on synthetic (hand-crafted) trajectory data, (c) residual-stacking detection works on synthetic residual histories, (d) the output JSON is well-formed and contains all required sections.
acceptance_criteria: A new file back/tools/audit_drift.py exists and is executable via `python back/tools/audit_drift.py --days 30`.
Running `python back/tools/audit_drift.py --days 30` completes without error and produces a JSON file in back/tools/audit_outputs/.

The output JSON contains a 'trajectories' object with keys for all 7 state fields and all 6 growth fields, each containing an array of per-day values with length equal to the number of simulated days plus the seed day.
The output JSON contains a 'residual_stacking' object with a per-day array of residual counts and a 'verdicts' sub-object.
The output JSON contains a 'drift_verdicts' object with one entry per tracked dimension, each having a 'status' field (pass/warn/fail) and a 'reasons' array.
The output JSON contains a top-level 'summary' object with an 'overall_status' field (pass/warn/fail).
A new test file back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py exists.
All tests in back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py pass via `python -m pytest back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py -v`.
The test file includes at least one test that verifies monotonic-drift detection flags a synthetic trajectory that moves in one direction for 10+ consecutive days.
The test file includes at least one test that verifies saturation-lock detection flags a synthetic trajectory stuck at ceiling for 5+ consecutive days.
The test file includes at least one test that verifies residual-stacking detection flags monotonically non-decreasing residual counts over 7+ consecutive days.
The test file includes at least one end-to-end test that runs the audit for 30 days on the deterministic backbone and verifies the output JSON structure.
All existing tests pass: `python -m pytest back/tests/ -v` has no regressions.
non_goals: Do not fix or tune any drift patterns found — this task is observation and reporting only.
Do not add new fields to any Pydantic domain model.
Do not extend the bridge to deferred ticks (T3/T5/T6/T7/T8).
Do not implement LLM-based appraisal or narrative analysis.
Do not modify the DegradationTracker or any appraisal infrastructure.
Do not add player-guidance scenarios — the audit runs with guidance=none.
Do not produce a markdown report — JSON output is sufficient (the existing audit_run.py already covers markdown reporting).
constraints: The audit tool must use the existing advance_day / simulate_day pipeline — do not build a parallel simulation loop.
The audit tool must be a pure observer — it must not modify any engine, domain model, or settlement logic.
All drift-detection logic must be pure functions operating on collected trajectory arrays — no side effects, no LLM calls.
The DegradationTracker is optional — the audit must work with or without one. When absent, the degradation-trend section is omitted from the report.
Residual data must be read from DaySnapshot.pending_residuals — do not invent a new residual tracking mechanism.
AppraisalSignal v1 is frozen — do not modify its field definitions.
Do not modify any existing engine files, domain models, or test files.
Output files go into back/tools/audit_outputs/ consistent with the existing audit_run.py convention.
review_focus: Verify drift-detection pure functions are correct: monotonic detection should not false-positive on oscillating values, saturation detection should correctly handle values that briefly dip below threshold.
Verify residual stacking reads from DaySnapshot.pending_residuals correctly and counts are accurate.
Verify the audit tool does not import or instantiate any LLM client — it should work purely on the deterministic backbone unless an optional tracker is injected.
Verify no forbidden files were modified.
Verify test coverage includes edge cases: empty trajectories, single-day runs, exactly-at-threshold values.
Verify JSON output is self-contained and machine-parseable — no embedded markdown, no prose-only sections.

execution_evidence.summary: Implemented P33-T5: Multi-day drift audit tool. Created back/tools/audit_drift.py as a pure-observer CLI that runs N simulated days via the existing advance_day pathway and detects monotonic drift, unbounded growth, saturation/floor lock, and residual stacking across all 13 tracked dimensions (7 AgentState + 6 AgentGrowth fields). Created back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py with 44 tests covering all detection functions (unit), the dimension-verdict builder, the residual-verdict builder, and a class-scoped end-to-end 30-day run that validates JSON structure. All 44 new tests pass; full suite of 1061 tests passes with no regressions.

back/tools/audit_drift.py.description: Drift audit CLI. Key functions: reset_to_seed, extract_state_values, extract_growth_values, extract_residual_info (pure data extraction), detect_monotonic_drift, detect_unbounded_growth, detect_saturation_lock, detect_residual_stacking (pure drift-detection), build_dimension_verdict, build_residual_verdict (verdict builders), run_drift_audit (simulation + detection loop, callable from tests), main (CLI entry point). Output goes to back/tools/audit_outputs/drift_{label}.json. Accepts --days, --label, --monotonic-window, --unbounded-threshold, --saturation-ceiling, --saturation-floor, --saturation-lock-window, --residual-max-count, --residual-monotone-window.

back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py.description: Test classes: TestDetectMonotonicDrift (8 tests), TestDetectUnboundedGrowth (6 tests), TestDetectSaturationLock (6 tests), TestDetectResidualStacking (8 tests), TestBuildDimensionVerdict (4 tests), TestEndToEndAudit (8 tests, class-scoped fixture runs 30-day backbone simulation once), TestBuildResidualVerdict (3 tests). Covers all acceptance criteria including synthetic trajectory checks and full JSON-structure validation.

met_criteria: 1. back/tools/audit_drift.py exists and runs via `python back/tools/audit_drift.py --days 30`
2. Tool completes without error and produces drift_*.json in back/tools/audit_outputs/
3. 'trajectories' contains all 7 state fields + 6 growth fields, each with 31 data points (seed + 30 days)

9. test_rising_10_consecutive_days_flagged and test_falling_10_consecutive_days_flagged verify 10+ day monotonic detection
11. test_monotone_nondecreasing_7_days_flagged verifies residual stacking over 7+ consecutive days

non_blocking_suggestions: test_all_zeros_not_flagged is misleadingly named — the test body correctly asserts flagged_monotone=True (zeros ARE flagged), but the test name implies no flags. Rename to test_all_zeros_flagged_monotone_but_not_max_exceeded for clarity.

detect_monotonic_drift sets streak_start = i-1 when a new direction begins, which can cause reported start_idx to be off by one when preceded by a flat value. This does not affect detection correctness but can produce slightly inaccurate span boundaries in the JSON report.

The saturation_lock window parameter in build_dimension_verdict defaults to saturation_lock_window=5, which matches the default ceiling/floor thresholds. Consider adding a note that the defaults were chosen against the known [7, 93] model value range.
review_verdict.rationale: All 13 acceptance criteria are satisfied. The new files (audit_drift.py, test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py) are the only changes — no existing files were modified. The drift-detection pure functions are algorithmically correct: monotonic detection uses sign-of-delta and correctly breaks streaks on oscillations or flat steps (no false positives on oscillating trajectories confirmed). Saturation-lock detection correctly resets streak count on any dip below threshold (strict consecutive behavior). Residual stacking reads from DaySnapshot.pending_residuals with correct count extraction. No LLM imports or clients are present. Test coverage includes edge cases: empty inputs, single-value inputs, exactly-at-threshold values (|30| is NOT > 30), and exact-window-length streaks. The JSON output is pure machine-readable JSON with no embedded markdown. The full test suite (1061 tests) passes with zero regressions.

claude_output_truncated:
All tasks complete. Here's what was implemented:

**`back/tools/audit_drift.py`** — pure-observer CLI (310 lines):
- Uses existing `advance_day` pathway — no parallel simulation loop
- Collects per-day snapshots of all 7 `AgentState` fields + all 6 `AgentGrowth` fields + `pending_residuals` count
- Four pure drift-detection functions: `detect_monotonic_drift`, `detect_unbounded_growth`, `detect_saturation_lock`, `detect_residual_stacking`
- Outputs JSON with `trajectories`, `drift_verdicts` (per-dimension `pass/warn/fail`), `residual_stacking`, and `summary.overall_status`
- All thresholds configurable via CLI flags
- `run_drift_audit()` extracted as a standalone callable for test access

**`back/tests/test_p33_t5_drift_audit.py`** — 44 tests across 7 classes:
- Unit tests for each detection function on synthetic data
- End-to-end `TestEndToEndAudit` (class-scoped fixture runs 30 days once, 8 structural checks)
- Covers all acceptance criteria: monotonic flagging, saturation-lock flagging, residual-monotone flagging, JSON schema

**Results**: 44/44 new tests pass, 1061/1061 total suite passes, zero regressions.
